generic_sampling_rules.int_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1; unique; never NULL. Generated PKs are appended above the compact max; compact PKs are never renumbered or changed.
generic_sampling_rules.int_fk: With probability 0.15 emit NULL when the column is nullable; otherwise copy a parent key drawn uniformly from the FINAL parent key set (compact parent keys + generated parent keys actually written to the instance). Never emit an orphan: every non-NULL value must be in the final parent key set. Assert this in the sampler. Unmatched-join coverage comes only from NULL child FKs and parent rows with no children.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Sample uniformly from the enumerated pool; with probability 0.1 emit a case/whitespace near-variant of a pool value.
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: Sample from a small pool of realistic strings; with probability 0.2 emit a near-duplicate (case change, extra space, accent variant) of an existing value.
generic_sampling_rules.real_rate: Sample uniformly in [0,1] rounded to 2 decimals; with probability 0.1 emit NULL if nullable; with probability 0.15 emit a value equal to another row's value (tie).
generic_sampling_rules.real_measure: Sample uniformly in the observed range rounded to 1 decimal; with probability 0.1 emit NULL if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.date_text: Sample from a small pool of date-range strings in the observed format; with probability 0.1 emit a near-variant (different separator or spacing).
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: For each column with a listed literal, include at least one row at the literal and one row one step on each side (numbers by step 0.01 for rates, 1 for ints; dates by one day).
generic_sampling_rules.tie: For each ORDER column, ensure at least two non-NULL rows share the value at the listed rank.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, at least one NULL row; NULL share equals the compact database's share for that column. Columns with zero compact NULLs receive zero generated NULLs unless listed in null_targets. Columns listed in null_targets get a NULL share of 5-30%. NOT NULL / PK columns never get NULL. A planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule.
generic_sampling_rules.final_verification: Run domain enforcement (rate/measure ranges, sex, dob) BEFORE the final verification pass, or run the verification pass again after enforcement and dedup. Assert every per_column_exceptions target holds on the written rows.

targets.reserve_parent_key: Reserve at least one people.People_ID and exclude it from FK draws so at least one parent row has no children by construction; verify in the final pass.

targets.non_null_share: candidate.People_ID must have a mix of NULL and non-NULL values; non-NULL FKs must match existing people rows (report match rate per instance).

targets.qualifying_rows: >= 2 per real group with different values; exclude NULL and orphan FK rows from grouping

dependencies.note: Draw from final parent key set (compact + generated). Compact people PKs are preserved; generated PKs appended above compact max.

semantic_rules_and_formulas.evidence: observed values M,F; boundary target also plants 'f', legal under case-insensitive predicate

generation_specification.uncertainty: The four rates are sampled independently: no cross-column sum or ordering constraint is asserted (shown rows do not sum to 1: row1 ~1.18, row2 ~1.81). The hard FOREIGN KEY cannot be waived; orphan FK rows are not generated. Unmatched-join coverage comes from NULL child FKs plus at least one reserved parent key with no children (constructed and verified). FK sampling must use the final parent key set actually written (compact PKs preserved, generated PKs appended above compact max); assert every non-NULL FK is in that set and report the non-NULL match rate. The Sex boundary variant 'f' is reconciled with the enum by LOWER(Sex) IN ('m','f'). Domain enforcement must run before the final verification pass (or the pass must re-run after enforcement/dedup) so clamping cannot destroy re-planted group-size, tie, duplicate, boundary or different-value patterns; assert all per_column_exceptions targets on the written rows.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: all 20 units failed with KeyError('People_ID') (n_ok=0, n_fail=20, errors: {KeyError: 20}). In instance.py build_random_instance, for table 'candidate' the FK column People_ID is excluded from samplers (it is in schema.fks), so cols does not contain 'People_ID' after the initial comprehension. _fk_from_parents is called with cols lacking People_ID and only iterates over cm.name in cols, so it never adds People_ID. Then _plant_nulls iterates over all columns and does cols[cm.name][i] = None for nullable columns; since People_ID is nullable (not notnull, pk_pos==0) and not in cols, this raises KeyError('People_ID').
issues.requested_revision: Ensure FK columns are present in cols before _plant_nulls/_plant_orphan_fks run. E.g. in _fk_from_parents, always set cols[cm.name] for every FK column (not only when cm.name in cols), or initialize cols with all table columns (including FK columns) before calling _fk_from_parents. Re-run generation and confirm n_ok>0 with no KeyError.

issues.evidence: Specification semantic rule: 'Support_rate + Consider_rate + Oppose_rate + Unsure_rate BETWEEN 0.9 AND 1.1' with evidence row1 sums to ~1.18 and row2 to ~1.81. The stated band [0.9,1.1] is contradicted by the cited evidence rows (1.18 and 1.81 both fall outside it). The uncertainty note acknowledges the sum is not tightly constrained but the formula still asserts a band that the evidence does not support.
issues.requested_revision: Either remove the sum-band rule (it is not supported by the shown rows) or widen it to a band that actually contains the observed sums (e.g. [0.9, 2.0]) and state the evidence consistently. Do not keep a formula whose own cited evidence violates it.

issues.evidence: instance.py _enforce_sum_band adjusts Consider_rate to force the sum into [0.9,1.1], but the specification's own evidence rows (1.18, 1.81) violate this band, so the enforcement contradicts the observed data and the (unsupported) rule. Additionally, _enforce_sum_band runs after _plant_nulls but the NULL rule says a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule; the code skips rows where any operand is None, which is consistent, but the band itself is the problem.
issues.requested_revision: Align _enforce_sum_band with the corrected specification (remove or widen the band). If the band is removed, delete the enforcement; if widened, use the corrected bounds.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_group_sizes sets vals[0]=vals[1]=vals[2]=base and vals[3..5]=base, producing a group of size >=6 for the base value, not the required '1, 2 and >= 3' distinct group sizes. It does not create a size-1 group and a size-2 group separately; all of indices 0-5 share base. Also for numeric base it sets vals[i]=base+i for i>=6, which may collide with base for i where base+i equals another value, and for candidate.Support_rate (a rate column) this can push values outside [0,1] before _enforce_rate_ranges clamps them, potentially collapsing distinct values.
issues.requested_revision: Rewrite _plant_group_sizes to explicitly create one group of size 1, one of size 2, and one of size >=3 (distinct values), respecting the column's domain (rates in [0,1], etc.). Verify group-size targets hold after all subsequent enforcement steps (ranges, ties, boundaries) which can overwrite the planted values.

issues.evidence: Ordering of planting steps in build_random_instance: _plant_group_sizes, _plant_ties, _plant_boundaries, then _enforce_rate_ranges/_enforce_measure_ranges/_enforce_sex/_enforce_dob/_enforce_sum_band/_enforce_different_values, then sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates. Later steps can overwrite values planted for earlier patterns (e.g. _enforce_sex maps non-M/F to 'M', destroying _plant_boundaries' 'f' and 'F ' variants; _enforce_rate_ranges clamps values that _plant_ties set to max; drop_unique_duplicates can drop rows that carried planted patterns). The specification requires these patterns to hold in the generated instance.
issues.requested_revision: Reorder so that domain enforcement (ranges, sex, dob, sum band) runs before pattern planting (ties, boundaries, group sizes, duplicates, different-values), or re-verify each pattern after enforcement and re-plant if violated. Ensure boundary variants ('F','f','F ') survive _enforce_sex (currently 'f' and 'F ' are mapped to 'M').

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_boundaries for people.Sex sets vals[0]='F', vals[1]='f', vals[2]='F '. But _enforce_sex later maps any value not in ('M','F') to 'M', so 'f' and 'F ' become 'M'. The comparison_boundary target requires values ['F','f'] to be present. After enforcement only 'F' and 'M' remain, so the 'f' boundary is lost.
issues.requested_revision: Make _enforce_sex preserve the boundary variants (e.g. allow case/whitespace variants of 'F'/'M' as valid, or run boundary planting after _enforce_sex). Confirm the generated instance contains both 'F' and 'f'.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_orphan_fks computes parent_vals from schema.original_values and cols.get(cm.name) (the child's own FK values), not from the parent's generated values. It then picks orphan = hi+1+randint(0,5). But _fk_from_parents already drew FK values from parent compact+generated; the orphan is planted after, overwriting one row. However _plant_parent_without_children and the final FK re-check loop (for self-referencing FKs only) do not re-validate that the orphan remains unmatched. More importantly, the orphan value hi+1+randint may coincidentally equal a generated parent key if parent keys were assigned sequentially above compact max (via _fresh_primary_keys), since parent keys start at max(compact)+1. So the 'orphan' can actually match a generated parent row, defeating the unmatched-join target.
issues.requested_revision: Compute the orphan value against the full parent key set (compact + generated parent keys for this instance), not just compact values, and choose a value guaranteed absent from that set. Verify unmatched_join_rows holds in the written instance.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_parent_without_children only checks schema.original_values for used child FK values, not the generated child rows in the current instance. Since generated candidate rows draw People_ID from parent compact+generated values, a parent key may be used by a generated child even if unused in compact data, so the 'parent rows without children' target may not hold.
issues.requested_revision: After generating child rows, compute the set of parent keys actually referenced by generated children and ensure at least one parent key is not referenced. Re-verify parent_rows_without_children in the written instance.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_nulls applies the NULL rule to every nullable column, including candidate.People_ID and candidate.Oppose_rate (flagged) but also others. However _fk_from_parents already assigns NULLs to FK columns with share _null_share_for, and then _plant_nulls re-samples NULL indices independently, so the final NULL share for People_ID is a combination and may exceed the 5-30% target or the compact share. Also _plant_nulls runs before _plant_orphan_fks, which overwrites a random row's FK with an orphan (non-NULL), potentially reducing NULL count below the required >=1.
issues.requested_revision: Apply the NULL rule once, after all other planting, and verify the final NULL share for each nullable column is within the target (5-30% for flagged columns, compact share otherwise) with at least one NULL row. Ensure orphan planting does not overwrite the only NULL row.

issues.evidence: instance.py _enforce_different_values only ensures the first two non-NULL values differ; it does not guarantee '>= 2 qualifying rows per group with different values' for the aggregate groups implied by the queries (e.g. per people.Sex group). The target is per-group, but the code operates globally on the column.
issues.requested_revision: Implement per-group different-value planting: for each group (e.g. by people.Sex for AVG(candidate.unsure_rate)), ensure at least two rows with different values. Verify against the group definition used by the queries.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_ties sets the two extreme values to max(nonnull) for numeric columns, but for candidate.Support_rate and candidate.Unsure_rate the subsequent _enforce_rate_ranges clamps to [0,1] (fine) and _enforce_different_values may then change one of the tied values (it changes vals[j] if vals[i]==vals[j]), breaking the tie at rank 1. Order of operations: _plant_ties then _enforce_different_values, so the tie can be destroyed.
issues.requested_revision: Run _plant_ties after _enforce_different_values, or make _enforce_different_values avoid the tied extreme rows. Verify ties at rank 1 for all TIE_TARGETS columns in the written instance.

issues.evidence: instance.py _fresh_primary_keys assigns sequential PKs above compact max, but _plant_parent_without_children may shift a parent PK to hi+1+randint(0,5) where hi is max of used child FK values (compact only), which can collide with the sequential PK range or with another shifted PK, and sample_fresh_primary_keys later drops duplicate PK tuples, reducing row count and potentially removing planted patterns.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure PK assignment and parent-without-children shifting produce unique PKs without dropping rows. Verify final row counts match table_sizes_per_instance (people 9, candidate 6) or document that appended rows are additional.

issues.evidence: Specification table_sizes_per_instance: people 9, candidate 6. But the program (instance.py choose_table_sizes) generates sizes via rand_lin or level sizes (30*rand to 200+), and build_random_instance is called with size=None, so generated instances have far more than 9/6 rows. The specification's table_sizes_per_instance is not implemented; the program appends many rows to the compact DB.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify whether table_sizes_per_instance refers to the compact DB (9/6) or the generated instance. If generated instances should match these sizes, pass size explicitly. If appended rows are intended, update the specification to state the generated row counts and remove the misleading table_sizes_per_instance or relabel it as compact sizes.

issues.evidence: writer.py write_instance_sqlite copies the compact DB and appends generated rows, but the generated rows use fresh PKs above compact max, so compact rows are preserved (good). However, if a generated row fails a constraint it is skipped and counted, but the code does not report which patterns were lost. Given the KeyError bug, no rows were written at all (n_ok=0).
issues.requested_revision: After fixing the KeyError, verify rows_added equals the intended generated row count per table and rows_skipped is 0. Report per-pattern verification (ties, group sizes, nulls, orphans) in the execution feedback.

unresolved_checks: Could not verify integrity constraints (PK uniqueness, FK consistency) in written instances because generation failed with KeyError before any instance was produced.
Could not verify preservation of compact rows or dependent-value consistency in output because n_ok=0.
Could not verify reproducible generation (seed determinism) because no instances were written.

The sum-band rule's evidence is internally inconsistent (cited rows 1.18 and 1.81 violate the stated [0.9,1.1] band); needs designer clarification before the rule can be validated.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports fk_violations=1563 across 20 instances (19/20 invalid, reason 'new_integrity_failures'). The generator deliberately plants orphan FK rows: instance.py `_plant_orphan_fks` overwrites a non-NULL candidate.People_ID slot with `orphan = hi + 1` (a key absent from the parent set), and `_plant_parent_without_children` shifts a parent PK above every used key. writer.py inserts with `pragma foreign_keys = OFF`, so these orphans are written silently. The schema declares `FOREIGN KEY (People_ID) REFERENCES people(People_ID)`, so every instance with a planted orphan violates the FK constraint.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the unmatched_join_rows target with the declared FK constraint. Either (a) drop the planted orphan-FK rows and satisfy 'unmatched_join_rows' only via parent-rows-without-children (which does not violate FK), or (b) if orphan child rows are genuinely required, the specification must explicitly state that FK integrity is intentionally relaxed and the validity checker must be told so. As written, the program produces databases that fail the schema's own integrity constraints, which is a blocking error. Also stop disabling `foreign_keys` in writer.py so violations surface rather than being hidden.

issues.evidence: The specification's `int_fk` rule says 'with probability 0.15 emit NULL when the column is nullable; otherwise a parent key; plant exactly one orphan ... when the unmatched_join_rows pattern requires it.' But the schema's FK is a hard constraint; the atomic-operation target `unmatched_join_rows` lists `child_rows_with_null_fk: true` and `parent_rows_without_children: true` but does not authorize FK-violating orphan rows. The spec conflates 'unmatched join rows' (achievable via NULL FK + parent-without-children) with 'orphan FK values' (which violate the FK).
issues.requested_revision: Clarify that unmatched_join_rows is satisfied by NULL foreign keys and parent rows without children only, and remove the 'plant exactly one orphan' instruction, OR explicitly document that FK enforcement is waived for this dataset and update the integrity expectations accordingly. The two interpretations must not both be present.

issues.evidence: The NULL rule is applied inconsistently. `_plant_nulls` is documented as 'applied once, last' and 'never replace a NULL', but `_fk_from_parents` already injects NULLs into candidate.People_ID at the compact share, and `_plant_orphan_fks` then overwrites a non-NULL slot with an orphan. More importantly, the feedback shows people.Date_of_Birth NULL 143/1440, people.Height 151/1440, people.Name 140/1440, people.Weight 159/1440, candidate.Consider_rate 179/1690, candidate.Support_rate 19/1690, candidate.Unsure_rate 141/1690 — i.e. NULLs are being generated in columns that the compact database may not have had NULLs in, and the shares are not clearly 'the compact database's share'. The spec's `null_targets` only lists candidate.People_ID and candidate.Oppose_rate, yet many other columns receive NULLs.
issues.requested_revision: Verify the compact NULL share per column and ensure `_plant_nulls` uses exactly that share (clamped only for the two flagged columns). Columns with zero compact NULLs should get zero generated NULLs unless the spec explicitly flags them. The current behavior injects NULLs broadly (e.g. people.Name, people.Height) which is not justified by the specification.

issues.evidence: `_enforce_sum_band` adjusts Consider_rate to force the sum into [0.9, 2.0], but the specification's formula is conditional on 'Oppose_rate IS NOT NULL AND Unsure_rate IS NOT NULL' and the evidence only shows two rows (1.18, 1.81). The band [0.9, 2.0] is a widened guess ('the band is widened to [0.9,2.0] to contain the observed sums'), not a supported rule. Enforcing it by mutating Consider_rate can destroy the group-size and different-value patterns planted earlier (the code re-applies rate ranges but not group sizes/ties after the sum-band step).
issues.requested_revision: Either drop the sum-band formula (it is uncertain, based on 2 rows) or, if kept, re-plant group sizes/ties/different-values after `_enforce_sum_band` and document the band as a soft/uncertain rule. The current ordering can silently break the group_sizes and ties_for_order_limit targets for candidate.Consider_rate-adjacent columns.

issues.evidence: `_plant_group_sizes` for candidate.Support_rate and candidate.Unsure_rate (rate columns) uses `_var(k) = round(base + 0.05*(k+1), 2)` clamped to [0,1]. If base is near 1.0, all variants clamp to 1.0 and the '1, 2, >=3' group sizes collapse to a single group. Similarly `_plant_ties` sets the two largest non-NULL values to the max, which for a rate column can push the value to 1.0 and then `_enforce_rate_ranges` (re-applied) keeps it, but the tie may be destroyed if the max was already 1.0 and another row also 1.0 — acceptable, but the group-size collapse is a real risk.
issues.requested_revision: Make `_plant_group_sizes` robust to clamping: choose base values that leave room for distinct variants (e.g. base in [0.1, 0.6]) or verify after planting that three distinct groups exist and re-plant if not. Add a post-plant verification step for all group_sizes and ties targets, as the docstring claims ('verified; any pattern destroyed ... is re-planted') but the code does not actually verify.

issues.evidence: The specification's `semantic_rules_and_formulas` includes `Support_rate + Consider_rate + Oppose_rate + Unsure_rate BETWEEN 0.9 AND 2.0` with evidence from only two rows, and `Sex IN ('M','F')` while the boundary target requires 'F' and 'f' (case variant). The `_enforce_sex` function preserves 'f' as a valid value, but the formula `Sex IN ('M','F')` would be FALSE for 'f' under SQLite's case-sensitive comparison. This is a contradiction between the formula and the boundary target.
issues.requested_revision: Either state the Sex formula as case-insensitive (`LOWER(Sex) IN ('m','f')`) or drop the 'f' boundary variant. The current spec has an internal inconsistency: the formula excludes 'f' but the boundary target requires it.

issues.evidence: `_enforce_different_values` builds a `lookup` from `inst.get(gt, {}).get('People_ID', [])` zipped with `gvals = inst.get(gt, {}).get(gc, [])`. For the candidate table, `gt='people'`, `gc='Sex'`, so `gvals` is people.Sex and the zip key is people.People_ID — correct. But the fallback `groups[i] = str(child)` when the child FK is not in the lookup means orphan/NULL FK rows get grouped by their raw FK value, which is not a real Sex group. This can cause the different-value check to operate on spurious groups.
issues.requested_revision: Skip rows whose FK is NULL or orphan when computing per-group different-value requirements, or map them to a sentinel group that is excluded from the check. The current fallback can mask a real failure to produce >=2 different values per actual Sex group.

issues.evidence: `build_random_instance` calls `_enforce_rate_ranges(schema, t, cols) if (t, cm_name_in(cols, RATE_RANGES, t)) else cols` — `cm_name_in` returns a column name (truthy string) or None, so the condition is effectively 'does table t have any rate column'. This re-applies rate ranges to ALL rate columns after planting, which can clamp values that `_plant_ties`/`_plant_group_sizes` set to exactly 1.0 (fine) but also re-rounds values, potentially breaking the tie at rank 1 if two rows were set to the same max and one gets re-rounded differently. Minor, but the guard is misleading.
issues.requested_revision: Replace the `cm_name_in` guard with a direct check `any((t, c.name) in RATE_RANGES for c in tm.columns)` and ensure re-application is idempotent (it is, since clamping to [0,1] of an already-in-range value is a no-op). The current code is functionally OK but the guard is confusing and should be simplified.

issues.evidence: Construction feedback: `construction_pairs: eligible 55, separated 16`. 39 of 55 eligible pairs are not separated. The instructions note a missing separation alone does not prove an error, but combined with the FK violations and the group-size collapse risk, the value variation is not reliably achieving the intended distinctions. The `_plant_group_sizes` and `_plant_ties` functions are applied per-table in a fixed order and can overwrite each other (e.g. `_plant_ties` sets two rows to max, then `_plant_group_sizes` overwrites rows 0-5 with group values, potentially destroying the tie).
issues.requested_revision: Add a final verification pass that checks each target pattern (group_sizes, ties, duplicates, boundaries, different_values) on the final column lists and re-plants any that were destroyed, as the docstring promises. The current pipeline order (ties -> group_sizes -> boundaries -> different_values -> duplicates -> orphan -> parent_without_children -> nulls) means later steps can destroy earlier patterns without re-planting.

unresolved_checks: Whether the compact database actually has NULLs in people.Name, people.Height, people.Weight, people.Date_of_Birth, candidate.Consider_rate, candidate.Support_rate, candidate.Unsure_rate — the feedback shows generated NULLs in these columns but the spec's null_targets only lists candidate.People_ID and candidate.Oppose_rate. The compact NULL shares were not provided in the input, so this cannot be fully verified.
Whether the sum-band [0.9, 2.0] is a real constraint or an over-generalization from two rows; the spec itself calls it 'widened' and 'uncertain'.

Whether the 16/55 separated construction pairs are due to the FK violations (orphan rows changing join results) or genuine value-variation gaps; the feedback does not break down which pairs failed and why.

Whether `_plant_parent_without_children` shifting a parent PK above all used keys can collide with a generated child FK that was drawn from the parent's generated values (the child FK list is built before the parent PK is shifted, so a child may reference the old PK value which is now orphaned — this is a second source of FK violations beyond the explicit orphan planting).

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: rows_added candidate=85, rows_skipped candidate=1605 across 20 instances (~95% of generated candidate rows rejected). Integrity is clean (fk_violations=0, pk_duplicates=0), so the skips are constraint failures on insert. The writer (writer.py) inserts with `pragma foreign_keys = ON` and counts failures per row; the candidate table is the only one with skips, and candidate.People_ID is the FK. The FK sampler `_fk_from_parents` draws from `schema.original_values[(people, People_ID)]` plus `inst['people']['People_ID']`, but `_fresh_primary_keys` renumbers people.People_ID to `range(max(compact)+1, ...)` AFTER `_fk_from_parents` already ran for candidate (candidate is built after people in table_order, so it sees the renumbered keys — but the compact people rows still carry their original People_IDs, and the sampler mixes compact original values with the renumbered generated ones). Any candidate row whose People_ID was drawn from the compact original set that is not also a generated key, or vice-versa, becomes an orphan and is skipped. This is a real generation defect: the spec explicitly requires `orphan_child_rows: 0` and 'Never emit an orphan'.
issues.requested_revision: Make FK sampling consistent with the final parent key set actually written to the instance. Either (a) do not renumber people.People_ID away from the compact values (keep compact PKs and append fresh keys above the compact max, so both compact and generated keys are valid parents), or (b) build candidate only after people's final PK list is fixed and draw exclusively from that final list (compact + generated). Add an assertion in `_fk_from_parents` that every non-NULL FK value is in the final parent key set, and re-run to confirm rows_skipped.candidate == 0.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback nullable_columns: `candidate.People_ID: generated rows: NULL 89 / 89` — every generated candidate row has a NULL FK, so no generated candidate row ever references a parent. Combined with the 1605 skipped rows, the effective generated candidate population is tiny and the FK column carries no non-NULL variation. The spec's `unmatched_join_rows` target requires both `child_rows_with_null_fk: true` AND `parent_rows_without_children: true` with real matched rows; a 100% NULL FK means the join `candidate.people_id = people.people_id` never matches on generated rows, so the intended join/group/aggregate variation (e.g. AVG(unsure_rate) grouped by people.sex) cannot be exercised. `_plant_nulls` tops up to the target share but `_fk_from_parents` already produced NULLs at the same share, and the renumbering bug above means the non-NULL draws were mostly orphans that got skipped, leaving only the NULLs.
issues.requested_revision: After fixing the FK/parent-key consistency, verify that generated candidate rows contain a mix of NULL and non-NULL People_ID values (NULL share 5-30%, not 100%), and that at least some non-NULL FKs match existing people rows. Add a post-generation check that reports the non-NULL FK match rate per instance.

issues.evidence: Specification `semantic_rules_and_formulas` asserts `Support_rate BETWEEN 0 AND 1`, `Consider_rate BETWEEN 0 AND 1`, `Oppose_rate BETWEEN 0 AND 1`, `Unsure_rate BETWEEN 0 AND 1` with evidence 'all shown ... values in [0.17,0.33]' etc. The `uncertainty` note itself observes the four rates do not sum to 1 (row1 ~1.18, row2 ~1.81). The [0,1] bounds are supported by the shown values, but the spec does not state whether the rates are independent or whether any sum/ordering relation is intended. This is a genuine uncertainty, not an error, but it should be recorded so the engineer does not over-constrain (e.g. by forcing a sum-to-1 formula).
issues.requested_revision: Keep the per-column [0,1] bounds (supported), and explicitly document in the spec that no cross-column sum/ordering constraint is asserted, so the generator samples the four rates independently. No code change required beyond confirming independence.

issues.evidence: `_plant_parent_without_children` is a documented no-op ('This function is a no-op guard that never breaks FK integrity'). The spec target `parent_rows_without_children: true` is therefore not actively constructed; it relies on the natural situation. With people=9 and candidate=6 per instance, and candidate FKs mostly NULL/skipped, some people rows will incidentally have no children, but this is not guaranteed by construction and is not verified. The spec's own uncertainty note says 'the generation program must run a final verification pass over every per_column_exceptions target'.
issues.requested_revision: Either implement `_plant_parent_without_children` to guarantee at least one parent key is unused by generated children (e.g. reserve one parent key and exclude it from FK draws), or add it to `_verify_and_replant` as an explicit checked target. Document the chosen approach in the spec.

issues.evidence: `_verify_and_replant` re-plants group sizes, ties, duplicates, boundaries and different-values, but the final `_enforce_rate_ranges`/`_enforce_measure_ranges`/`_enforce_sex`/`_enforce_dob` calls run AFTER `_verify_and_replant`, and `sample_fresh_primary_keys`/`drop_unique_duplicates` run after that.
